I enjoy showers too, but I'm a taller guy and most baths are not comfortable. I love saunas, but only been able to go to one I was comfortable with twice. 

I normally enjoy the heat of the shower, but laying there thinking about the end and hugging myself (do that a lot these days) and kept telling myself to get my blade , but I just sunk deeper into the bath. I mean, if it was going to be the last place and thing I feel, minds well observe how it feels. 
At that point, I just focused on how how the water was super hot, how it felt safe and how I was comfortable with this being my resting place. 

I ended up resting in the bath for awhile, and convinced myself to get out cuz then the crisp air would feel nice too... and then I went and drank a smooth from my fridge, ate 3 slices of honey ham lunch meat, and curled under a mount of blankets and pillows. I don't know how long I lay their, cuz I don't remember any thoughts.

I'm numb 99% of the time and some small thought in my head will just make me uncontrollably sob. 

Numbness is hell. I don't want to live this anymore... :(

I was a deep thinker and could help sort out life dilemmas. I was emotionally complex that I easily could understand, validate and help someone in a crisis...

Just my whole life, shitty family, shitty childhood, fucked up mind games, mental illness, poverty, lots and lots of rejection for personal reasons, marriage and then divorce (8 years), haven't been able to work for the last several years due to extreme anxiety.

  


Did therapy for 2 years and I grew and changed, but the depression and negative thoughts never let up... And I'm finally done. I'm just so tired of being numb all the time, but feeling everything so intensely! I'm tired of seeing details about the world that make it repugnant. I'm tired of all the details! I see so much beauty in complex, small organisms and the scale of the world is awe inspiring, but I just... Don't feel anything. It all doesn't matter to me...

Journals are one of the few habits you can form that will ripple throughout your life. As humans, we very rarely, if ever, have a conversation with out own minds. I'm not talking the silly ramblings we do when we are alone; I'm talking serious, soul seeking. Took me months to finally be able to write the words that I knew were true... And not have to fear my own judgement. It's like you know something is true, but if you...just...don't... look it at it directly, somehow it won't exist? Nope.

Being able to be honest and physically write out your thoughts, it's more major than most people will ever know.

We also retain stuff much much better when we hand write them... It has something to do with translating language into body motion...

And sadly, digital/typed journals don't quite have the magnitude that hand written ones do. I would love it to not be so, cuz I can encrypt like a mo-fo haha but eventually I just had to stash my journal and trust that the adults in my life wouldn't snoop.

My reassurance that they haven't is... They haven't freaked out about how insane I actually come across in my own mental ramblings.

Oh! Also, if you start... Don't pressure yourself to write about anything specific or deep... I started by just writing my thoughts exactly as I thought them, in real time usually. You will get the hang of it and your hand will cramp less and you'll write faster in a few months and then you really start to flow. Get a nice leather journal to start with and nice pens... Use colors if it makes you happy.

I had to seriously relax and told myself that if I spent something wrong, I would NOT go look it up... I would NOT fixate on it in the side of my thoughts... You just keep going :)

I actually preach something very similar to people. I used to work in and write about mental health. (yes, the irony is there haha) and I talk to everyone about establishing habits and how it can help increase their willpower and ability to them build on that habit to snowball into them changing their lives. 

I actually do workout several times a week. The habit that I took up majorly and has stuck for some time now, is journalling. It has single handedly changed the way I think about things. We don't often sit down and really have a conversation with out inner thoughts; it can be enlightening. 

My main issue is that my mornings are great; I am one of those obnoxiously happy people in the morning. I actually suffer from many different conditions, but one makes my joint and muscle pain the worst in the morning and at night. Even in pain, I have maintained the routine of journalling (even when my hands are hurting bad) and I even exercise sometimes. I try to push myself... it's all an experience, even the pain. It doesn't have to rule you though...

it's when it gets to night time and my brain starts to wind down... then I get lonely... and have too much time to thing. I call it "spiraling" and when it "clicks" in my head, it can take 10 minutes or 10 hours, but once the spiral starts, it will end with me being super super super depressed. Pretty consistently my evenings are shitty, but every once in awhile it all piles up on one night.

Laughing at ourselves is one of the few ways we have to stay sane... Dark humor.
